title: Pre-Analysis — Duplex Outflow Valve Actuator Standard for the Four-Engine Extension
abstract: Closed work order that extended the duplex actuator standard to the four-engine fleet and established the second essential bus feed route on that airframe.

sections.objective: Establish whether the duplex outflow valve actuator standard, released for the twin-engine aircraft in 2018, could be extended to the four-engine fleet, and in particular whether a second essential bus feed can be run to the actuator position on that airframe without a new harness.
sections.findings_summary: It can, and the extension was approved. The four-engine essential panel carries a spare position on the opposite bus at the right rating, and the run from the panel to the actuator position follows an existing route with enough space for the additional cable. The clamping is the only physical difference: the four-engine duct run has two fewer support positions and needs cushioned clamps added rather than substituted. Two documentation findings. The removal task carries the duplex isolation warning correctly but its access panel list is written for the twin-engine floor arrangement and would be wrong on the four-engine aircraft. And the crew abnormal procedure describes manual control of the valve in terms that assume the regeared drive, which is what the standard fits, so the extension keeps the crew documentation consistent rather than splitting it.
sections.next_steps: Approve the four-engine effectivity extension. Correct the access panel list in the removal task for the four-engine floor arrangement. Issue the bulletin revision that carries the extended effectivity and the additional clamp positions.

evidence.similarity_note: Found by entity linking on the actuator and clamp part numbers the task calls out.

expected_findings.rationale: The removal task carries the duplex isolation warning correctly, which is the safety-critical part, but its access panel list is written for the twin-engine floor arrangement and does not match the four-engine aircraft.
expected_findings.resolution: Correct the access panel list for the four-engine effectivity.

evidence.similarity_note: Surfaced by similarity alone; the crew procedure and the modification share no identifier and are written for entirely different readers.

expected_findings.rationale: The crew abnormal procedure describes manual valve control in terms that assume the regeared drive introduced by this standard. Extending the effectivity keeps the two fleets on one procedure rather than splitting it, which is a benefit nobody had counted.
expected_findings.resolution: No change. Record the consistency as a supporting argument for the extension.

evidence.similarity_note: Found through the bulletin applicability, which at the time covered only the twin-engine aircraft.

expected_findings.rationale: The retrofit bulletin effectivity has to be widened and the additional clamp positions added, otherwise a four-engine operator following it would leave the second motor cable unsupported over two spans.
expected_findings.resolution: Issue the bulletin revision with the extended effectivity and the clamp positions.

type_data.conclusion: Closed. The extension is approved subject to the bulletin revision and the access panel correction.
